hypothesis: The selected 7,386-byte BITLSTM blend saves real fixture payload bytes on Mac and Linux without changing development-binary size; the packed Linux compressor and decoder may still change. Measure the complete release component delta against both prior and untouched controls.
source_rule: Copy pinned original Linux release source. Change only src/bit_head_weights.h embedded BF16 array and hash in each candidate, with identical 7,386-byte geometry, model code, online-learning threshold, transformer, dictionary, order, packer and build flags.
toolchain: Build all three packages serially on native Ubuntu x86-64 using Clang 18 and isolated GCC 13 headers. Baseline and prior packages must reproduce previously saved exact SHA-256 values.
comparison: Independently inspect saved comp9 and decoder-prefix bytes, compare complete release components and external blocks, and retain all positive or negative deltas. The payload gains do not authorize extrapolation to enwik9.
acceptance: All three original release packer self-check suites pass
Untouched and prior release package hashes reproduce their pinned values
Only the two declared BF16 source bindings differ from baseline, with unchanged non-code blocks
Save complete component sizes, hashes, binary artifacts and logs even if the blend loses at package level
limitations: Complete package components plus fixture payloads are not the full prize score
No full enwik9 payload, independent self-extracting decode or official resource adjudication is measured
The small fixtures are reused evaluation ranges, not unseen final validation
